name: bounded-memory-candidate-spec-before-broad-review-scans
title: Stop high-token reviewer scans with bounded memory preflight and candidate spec routing
description: Problem: current Proof-or-Stop reviewer prompts can force broad or full docs/requirements/decisions/*.md scans before using bounded recall or candidate selection, causing very high token spend across host accounts. Evidence gathered on 2026-07-09: docs/requirements/decisions currently has 112 Markdown files, about 331,141 words and 2,489,160 bytes; the scope-plan prompt tells reviewers to read every decision file, and behavior review also performs a full decisions-directory spec-boundary scan. Existing runtime already has non-authoritative Memory Runtime Preflight, dev_memory_preflight/search, and playbook runtime advisory wiring, but the high-token reviewer prompts do not consistently use those surfaces before broad scans. Goal: ship a stopgap prompt-and-test change that makes bounded memory/playbook preflight plus candidateSpecSet the default path before broad scans, while keeping full decisions scan available only as a recorded escalation path for high-risk lifecycle/gate/process-fact/global rename/candidate ambiguity/reviewer escalation. Non-goals: do not make memory/playbook gate evidence, do not weaken scope review, do not remove full scan capability, do not implement a full CLI metrics sink, and do not change lifecycle gates or DONE semantics.
source: user-request: token consumption is highest priority on 2026-07-09
